record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: Is a significant excess of direct low-energy photons produced in soft particle processes relative to the known background, mainly bremsstrahlung, and can positive WA83 evidence be reconciled with other experiments reporting negative results?

evidence.quote: More precisely, the question remains to know whether a significant excess of /it direct photons of low energy is produced with respect to the known background, mainly due to bremsstrahlung.

The results shown to us by the WA83 collaboration at CERN, see [4], give evidence for a strong excess, but amazingly similar in shape and properties with the bremsstrahlung. It is clear that this interesting experimental finding has to be confronted with other ones wich give negative results.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy hadronic collisions (for example π⁻p collisions at 280 GeV/c or pp collisions at 450 GeV/c), consider the spectrum of "direct" low-energy (soft) photons produced in association with the produced charged hadrons, defined as the inclusive photon yield with transverse momentum well below typical hadronic scales (roughly p_T ≲ 50 MeV/c), after subtraction of photons originating from decays of produced hadrons. The standard theoretical background is the inner bremsstrahlung from accelerated external charged particles, computed e.g. via the low-energy (Low) theorem from the measured hadronic amplitude.

(a) Determine whether the inclusive yield of direct soft photons in such soft hadronic processes exhibits a statistically significant excess over the inner-bremsstrahlung prediction.

(b) Reconcile experimental measurements that report a strong excess (of order several times the bremsstrahlung expectation, with a spectral shape and kinematic dependence closely resembling bremsstrahlung) with other experiments at comparable energies that report no significant excess; i.e., identify a single physical mechanism (and/or systematic effect in the background calculation or photon detection) consistent with all reported results.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews (2024) describe the anomalous soft photon excess observed in WA83, WA91, WA102, DELPHI and related experiments as still unexplained: multiple experiments confirm excesses of factors ~4–8 over inner bremsstrahlung with bremsstrahlung-like spectral shape, while no generally accepted theoretical mechanism reconciles all measurements, and tensions with experiments reporting null or weaker signals persist. The question therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Anomalous soft photons: status and perspectives
status_evidence.snippet: Several experiments observed soft photon signals exceeding predicted hadronic bremsstrahlung rates by several times; the effects still lack a theoretical explanation.
status_evidence.claim: The soft photon excess remains unexplained as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: Anomalous soft photons (Physics Reports)
status_evidence.snippet: No model has been able to give a consistent description of the events as a whole; generally accepted theories of soft photon production beyond QED bremsstrahlung are nonexistent.
status_evidence.claim: No accepted theory reconciles the experimental results.
